description: Water use looks wrong in one irrigation zone, and the operator needs to reconstruct when the anomaly began, under what conditions it appears, and whether it lines up with crop stress observations.

user_profile.persona: 38-year-old farm operations lead who watches both field conditions and equipment behavior
user_profile.context: The anomaly is not catastrophic yet, but it has become too persistent to dismiss as random variation
user_profile.communication_style: Diagnostic and observational, wants field evidence linked to equipment patterns

fact_sheet.fact: The area under investigation is Irrigation Zone 7B at Veridian Fields, which covers 40 acres of alfalfa.
The standard irrigation cycle for Zone 7B is programmed in the AgriLogic Suite to deliver 2.5 acre-inches of water over a 6-hour period.
Since June 18, 2024, the AgriLogic Suite has logged an average water usage of 3.8 acre-inches per cycle for Zone 7B.
The farm operations lead investigating the issue is Alex Torres.
On July 12, 2024, drone imagery from the AeroScout AG-4 showed NDVI values as low as 0.65 in the southwest corner of Zone 7B, indicating crop stress.
Healthy sections of alfalfa in the adjacent Zone 7A have a consistent NDVI reading of 0.82.
The primary flow meter for Zone 7B is Meter ID #7B-FM-01, a Mag-Meter model X2.
Flow meter #7B-FM-01 was last calibrated on April 5, 2024, by field technician Maria Garcia.
During anomalous cycles, the flow rate at meter #7B-FM-01 spikes from the target 800 GPM to 950 GPM for periods of 15-20 minutes.
System pressure at Pump Station Delta, which feeds Zone 7B, drops from a normal 55 PSI to 48 PSI during the flow rate spikes.
Soil moisture sensor #7B-SM-03, located in the stressed area, has recorded volumetric water content (VWC) reaching 42%, indicating oversaturation.
The target VWC for the alfalfa crop in Zone 7B is 35% before irrigation cutoff.
Log analysis shows that 8 out of the last 10 anomalous water usage events occurred when wind speeds recorded at Veridian Weather Station #2 exceeded 15 mph from the west.
A visual inspection by Maria Garcia on July 14, 2024, revealed a slow leak at the main gasket of valve assembly #7B-V-12.
Alex Torres created ticket #IRR-2024-113 for the leaking gasket in the AgriLogic Suite maintenance module on July 15, 2024.
The irrigation system in Zone 7B is an AquaFlow 5000 center pivot system.
The last preventative maintenance schedule for the AquaFlow 5000 pivot in Zone 7B was completed on March 20, 2024.
Maria Garcia's field notes from July 13, 2024, mention 'visible yellowing and standing water' near sprinkler head #104 on the pivot's outer span.
The irrigation control panel is an AquaFlow Control v3.2, accessible via the IP address 192.168.1.50 on the farm's internal network.
The cost of water is billed at $65 per acre-foot by the San Joaquin Water District.
The anomalous water usage represents an estimated excess operational cost of $150 per week for Zone 7B alone.
Alex Torres contacted David Chen, an external consultant from Precision Irrigation Solutions, on July 15, 2024, via email at d.chen@precision-irrigation.com for a second opinion.
The service log for Pump Station Delta shows no unscheduled shutdowns or pressure faults in the last 90 days.
The average daily evapotranspiration (ET) rate for the first two weeks of July was 0.25 inches, which is within the historical norm for the period.
The yellowing in the crop is consistent with symptoms of root hypoxia due to waterlogging, not nutrient deficiency.
The firmware version on the AquaFlow Control v3.2 panel is 3.2.1-build-20231102.
Veridian Fields' standard operating procedure, document #VF-IRR-004, requires a full system diagnostic if water usage deviates by more than 15% for three consecutive cycles.
The water usage deviation in Zone 7B has been approximately 52% (3.8 vs 2.5 acre-inches) for the past 14 irrigation cycles.
Maria Garcia's work phone number for urgent field dispatch is 555-018-2345.
The replacement part for the leaking gasket at valve assembly #7B-V-12 is a 'Model AF-G-300', with 3 units in stock in the main supply shed, bin C-4.
